the matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) MMP-9 from stromal cells contributes to tumor colonization and survival in the lung microenvirnment, and that this MMP is required for the survival but not growth rate of tumor cells.
MMP-9, but not MMP-7 or MMP-2, from bone marrow-derived stromal cells, contributes to the survival and establishment of metastatic lung cancer cells in the lung.

the role of MMP-9 in the development of lung tumors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MMP-9 is a critical determinant of the establishment and survival of tumor cells in experimental metastasis models.
stromal-derived MMP-9 from neutrophils contributes to survival of metastatic lung cancer cells but not to tumor growth.
stromal MMP-2, MMP-7 and MMP-9 are all involved in tumor cell growth, but only MMP-9 plays a role in tumor cell survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MMP-9 is a critical factor for lung tumor cell survival in the lung micro-environment, but it does not affect lung tumor cell growth.
MMPs play a significant role in the metastatic cascade, and the role of MMPs is different depending on the tissue microenvironment and the timing of their expression.
MMP-9 is important in the early survival of lung tumor cells in the microenvironment of the lung but has no effect on growth once the tumor has been established.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stromal MMPs are important for the survival of tumor cells in a premetastatic microenvironment, and this may be an important therapeutic target.
MMP-9 plays a role in early tumor colonization of the lung and that MMP-9 inhibitors may be more useful in the treatment of early-stage lung cancer.
stromal MMPs have an important function in the early stages of tumor establishment and metastasis, and targeting these enzymes in the early stages might provide a therapeutic benefit.
